notes.title: Decipher the Past: Introducing the Lexicon Engine
notes.content:
[h3]Greetings, Vikings![/h3]

In my ongoing mission to deepen immersion through dynamic systems design, I’m proud to unveil the [b]Lexicon Engine[/b] — a proprietary in-game language parsing and translation framework I’ve developed from the ground up in Unreal Engine. Designed for scalability and reuse across multiple projects, Lexicon enables player-driven language discovery, adaptive translation, and runtime text parsing to bring ancient languages to life in richly interactive worlds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/6f029b0f9b2d408911e4020c22fdaa559d228873.png[/img]

Much like the mechanic in No Man’s Sky, players will encounter ancient texts, scribbled notes, weathered carvings, and forgotten tomes written in one of three initial historical languages: Scottish Gaelic, Latin, and Anglo-Saxon (Old English).

But here’s the twist — you can only speak [u]Old Norse[/u].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/ab36b47f8801d8f9c37dc8d2e0578d4308ee47e4.png[/img]

[h2]Three Ancient Tongues, One Island of Secrets[/h2]

The island of Skye is steeped in forgotten history and fractured cultures. Across its wild terrain, you’ll discover texts and whispers from a lost world — but they won’t be in modern English. Just like a wayward soul awakening in an unfamiliar land, you’ll encounter these messages untranslated, obscure, and mysterious.

[h3]Supported Languages:[/h3]

[list]
[*] Scottish Gaelic – Native to the land and woven into druidic knowledge and oral tradition

[*] Latin – Found in monastic records, imperial relics, and ritual texts

[*] Anglo-Saxon (Old English) – Rare and hidden, often tied to a secretive Catholic Order buried deep beneath the politics of Portree
[/list]

And yes — Lexicon supports [b]Unreal's full localization toolset[/b]. Whether you play the game in German, French, or beyond, the system still functions seamlessly at runtime.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/07061bf7d470b342879ef0aa40125e70fbea270c.png[/img]

You’ll begin the game unable to understand any of these tongues. But over time, through exploration and observation, you’ll slowly learn to read and comprehend them — word by word.

[h2]Learn Through Discovery[/h2]

You won’t be handed instant translations. Instead, your knowledge of each language is earned and personalized. Here's how you'll piece them together:

[list]
[*] Find bilingual texts – Discover fragments that pair ancient language with English for comparison
[*] Speak to scholars and seers – Earn the trust of NPCs who may offer lessons or phrases
[*] Examine carvings and relics – Compare symbols across ruins, tools, and stone monuments
[*] Immerse yourself – Frequent reading builds pattern recognition, expanding your dictionary naturally
[/list]

Every word you learn is permanently remembered by the system. Slowly, passages begin to reveal themselves, unlocking secrets and storylines that were previously hidden.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/d5207cf51658364461827e22081d9956c24117d2.png[/img]

Whether you’re translating a monastic scroll or deciphering a grave warning etched into stone, Lexicon dynamically parses based on your understanding — showing full, partial, or completely obscured texts depending on your progress.

[h2]Why It Matters[/h2]

This system introduces a whole new layer of depth and meaning to exploration. It rewards the curious and observant. It’s not just about reading — it’s about [i]decoding[/i].

Mastering ancient languages opens new quest paths, hidden lore, and secret locations. Every piece of knowledge you gain changes how you perceive the world around you. In Skye, [b]knowledge is as powerful as steel[/b].

No two players will experience the lore the same way. Your journey is shaped by what you learn — and what you choose to pursue.

That scrawled prayer? It could be a threat. Or a cure. But only if you can understand it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/564e3e2400d50ea0882a90e220780f90fd328c8b.png[/img]

[h2]Behind the Scenes: Smart Parsing[/h2]

The Lexicon Engine tracks your knowledge across thousands of words in each language. As your dictionary expands, previously unreadable texts unlock new meanings — encouraging you to revisit old locations with fresh eyes.

The system also integrates with the new Player Journal, meaning forgotten stories, mysterious phrases, or undeciphered notes can suddenly become relevant again — and may even reveal new quests.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/216a7d2f6476381181f76c1e315c7bfedeb7f763.png[/img]

[h2]Closing Thoughts[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/3f5c0a31c67a626a02933f39e9b0ba39fc6a3ddd.png[/img]

I truly believe the Lexicon Engine can add something truly special to Skye: Rebirth — a sense of wonder, mystery, and personal growth that reflects the heart of this project.

It’s about earning understanding, not just unlocking content. It’s about the joy of discovery.
Let me know in the comments which language you’re most excited to master — or how you’d like to learn these ancient tongues.

Thanks for being part of this journey. I can’t wait to see the stories [i]you[/i] uncover when the Lexicon Engine goes live.

Until then — keep your eyes open, your mind sharp, and your axe close.

– Mark

notes.title: Navigating Like a True Viking in Skye: Rebirth
notes.content:
[h1]No Compass — Just the Wild[/h1]

Survival on the Isle of Skye isn’t just about strength — it’s about awareness.  
In the pursuit of deeper immersion, I’ve stripped away the usual crutches — no glowing waypoints, no hovering minimaps, no UI compass cluttering your view. Instead, you’ll navigate Skye the way our ancestors once did: by reading the land, the sky, and the quiet signs left behind.

This is a world where the elements speak. You just have to learn how to listen.

[h1]Nature As Your Compass[/h1]  
The world itself becomes your guide. Pay attention to the shape of hills, the arc of the sun, and the whispers of wind. Every clue is there — if you’re willing to see it.

[h2]Sun and Moon[/h2]  
Skye’s skies aren’t just pretty — they’re built around real-world latitude and longitude, with the Sun and Moon tracking across the sky just as they would in nature. Their paths shift with the seasons, reflecting solstices and equinoxes, offering a dependable way to stay oriented whether you’re wandering by day or navigating by starlight.

[h3]The Sun Rises in the East[/h3]  
Each day begins with light spilling from the east. But the sun doesn’t always rise from the same point — it drifts with the months, mimicking the rhythms of the real world.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/fd9b5e8fc4cadff60240c2ab3507905af278497f.png[/img]

[h3]And Sets in the West[/h3]  
By observing the sun’s position at sunrise or sunset, players can orient themselves with primitive markers — simple logs or stones placed with purpose. It’s a technique I learned myself, wild camping in the forests of Snowdonia.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/577d1dc238d6a7901b32907c22653c06f037f809.png[/img]

[h3]Moon rising in the East[/h3]  
The Moon, too, rises in the east and moves across the night sky — a silent guide in the dark.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/da11477e263b53ef5e5d209b5569ea4c5ae08f75.png[/img]

[h3]Buildings as Bearings[/h3]  
Not all signs are natural. Some structures — like churches — are aligned east-west. Stone circles, too, often point to the solstices. These can anchor you in unfamiliar terrain.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/8eb1c9d12a19124e428b398c43764acf8528fe66.png[/img]  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/74c97a683ff4348d28beab02ed71ef036fd5ecad.png[/img]

[h2]Navigate by the Stars[/h2]  
When night falls and the world goes quiet, the stars take over. Players familiar with the old ways can use constellations to find true north — follow Ursa Major to Polaris, and you’ll never lose your path.

[h3]A view of Polaris and Ursa Major[/h3]  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/9cc5a391a6750fa24e7ffec468905184345efd5c.png[/img]

[h2]Forests[/h2]  
Even moss tells stories — growing thickest on the north side of trees. A quiet cue in a noisy world.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/13d20eb49b92def6d968ed63bc87c539dcd7bfc0.png[/img]

[h2]Rivers[/h2]  
Rivers always move downhill — often toward the sea. Follow them and you may find life: freshwater, food, or signs of civilization.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/696d3947ca97a328685c023dbb50175738073879.png[/img]

[h2]Wind[/h2]  
Wind moves through the land like a spirit — and if you’re paying attention, it might guide you. Sometimes it carries the scent of smoke, or the sounds of distant creatures.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/6529123ea122f2cfc46e690b1408f06f093501e5.png[/img]

[h2]Distant smoke[/h2]  
Smoke itself is a sign — a thread on the horizon. It could mean a campfire, a safe haven... or something far more dangerous.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/e4131bc57759449692386581930ff62040702094.png[/img]  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/c51368236a3939dc11898c9d4202bda04e418f83.png[/img]

[h2]Tides[/h2]  
Tides rise and fall at predictable times. Watch the shoreline and you’ll learn when to search for wreckage, reveal hidden loot, or time your crossings. Some players even use the tide to tell time.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/2a7c2740efcfe2d2f6e25f75173a995a0b7b54ce.png[/img]  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/40323957a2a1b00d5a3dedd1e81297ee15bfe6cd.png[/img]

[h1]Watch the Wilds[/h1]  
The land is alive, and it speaks — if you know how to listen.

[h2]Birds[/h2]  
Flocks circle above sources of water. If you’re lost, look up.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/6afd6e55617b7d44ef8168759d4a87ccf8957bfc.png[/img]

[h2]Animal trails[/h2]  
Animals follow paths worn into the land. Some lead to water. Others to danger. Pay attention to where they tread — and what they avoid.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/947be34af14863e1436de6ff49a083d4ed8f990f.png[/img]  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/8487ab3ef10b9ef887f0505c059be0a9ad30ade6.png[/img]

[h1]Leave Your Mark[/h1]  
Not all paths are given — some you must make for yourself. These tools help you do just that.

[h2]Cardinal Marker[/h2]  
Built from logs and stone, these primitive markers can be aligned using the rising sun to fix your cardinal direction. A personal compass, born from patience and precision.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/b881e4ac2d2e0f680fa09dbe1740cd4662974e2b.png[/img]

[h2]Sunstone[/h2]  
Inspired by Viking legend, the Sunstone is a crystal that reveals the sun’s position even in heavy cloud. Craft one, and the light will never leave you lost.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/f1f9b308bf5033a6bd3c2369b77540178f9e4f49.png[/img]

[h2]Cairns[/h2]  
Stack stones to leave a message — for yourself or others. Cairns once marked graves, trails, and territories. Here, they can guide your return… or warn others away.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/8acb123e2c1e2be381b90d4ed6f1b64f0f1fba9a.png[/img]

[h2]Wooden Direction Markers[/h2]  
Crude wooden posts, marked with feathers, cloth, or bones. Spin them to point toward camp, treasure, or the unknown. A quiet language, written in wood.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/58b48bf60cdf14259a190dd3d3ca2ecd3e9dce74.png[/img]

[h2]Sundial[/h2]  
Craftable sundials let you track the hours using nothing but sun and shadow. Plan your journey. Time the tides. Chase the last light before nightfall.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/eb24fd20ca60343ae0358a2013ef3996d952dafe.png[/img]

[h2]Roadside Torches[/h2]  
Torches can now be placed anywhere in the world — not just inside your camp. Whether you're carving a path through the dark forest, marking a treacherous route across the cliffs, or simply lighting the way back home, these flames can become your lifeline.  

But fire doesn’t last forever. Torches now require fuel to stay alight, so use them wisely. A well-placed line of burning lights can guide you safely — or betray your path to those watching in the shadows.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/ffda6b681336d44311191ed1aed10dcb108057f9.png[/img]

These systems don’t exist just for realism — they’re here to reward attentiveness. If you engage with the world, the world will guide you. This is survival, not just in body — but in mind.

Just you, the land, and the way back home.

[h2]Closing Thoughts[/h2]  
This is just the beginning of the saga. As Skye: Rebirth continues to grow, I’ll keep building on these features — adding new content and deepening the world bit by bit.  

Thank you, as always, for walking this path with me. This update brings us one step closer to a world where every step matters, every shadow tells a story, and every player leaves their mark behind.  

Our journey has only just begun.  

Skål,  
Mark

notes.title: Skye: Rebirth - Armour & Clothing Overhaul
notes.content:
[h1]Showcase[/h1]

One of the biggest missing elements from Skye: The Misty Isle has now been fully implemented—armor and clothing! This long-awaited system brings far more than just visual customization; every piece of gear you equip will directly impact your character’s stats and survival capabilities. While this is still very much a work in progress this showcases collecting, equipping and stat changes within the upcoming clothing system.

[previewyoutube=80G97oiatBo;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]More Than Just Looks[/h2]

Clothing and armor in Skye are more than cosmetic. Every item you wear affects core player stats, including:

[list]
[*] Defense – Protects against physical damage from enemies and the environment.
[*] Stamina – Adjusts your endurance, affecting movement, attacks, and survival.
[*] Carry Weight – Heavier armor reduces mobility, but backpacks and belts increase inventory capacity.
[*] Body Temperature – Essential for surviving Skye’s dynamic weather; staying warm in harsh winters is just as crucial as keeping cool in summer.
[/list]

[h2]A Robust Expandable Equipment System[/h2]

With 84 pieces of wearable equipment, players can mix and match to suit their playstyle and survival needs. Equipment slots include:

[list]
[*] Arms
[*] Backpacks & Bags
[*] Bracers
[*] Boots
[*] Gloves
[*] Helmets
[*] Hoods
[*] Jewelry
[*] Trousers
[*] Shoulders
[*] Chest Pieces
[*] Capes
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/b1397b67fc2da7614cff3cedba84806c91f87eed.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/a3c6b98e8f6dd259073dd5855ffeb9d41c855e73.png[/img]

Every piece of gear plays a role in your survival, whether it’s a fur-lined cloak keeping you warm, a reinforced chest piece offering protection, or a sturdy pair of boots increasing movement efficiency.

[h2]Weight & Encumbrance System[/h2]

Armor comes with trade-offs. Heavier armor provides more protection but slows movement and drains stamina faster. Lighter clothing keeps you agile but offers less defense. Additionally, carrying too much clothing in your inventory increases encumbrance, forcing players to make strategic choices about what to bring on long journeys.

[h2]Layering & Weather Adaptation[/h2]

The harsh environment of Skye means that survival depends on proper clothing choices. Some outfits provide insulation against the cold (Fur), while others are better suited for wet (Leather) or humid conditions (Cotton). Wearing multiple layers—such as a wool tunic under a leather jerkin—helps regulate body temperature. However, getting caught in the rain while wearing heavy clothing can sap warmth, adding an extra survival challenge.

[h2]Clothing Degradation & Repair[/h2]

Survival isn't just about crafting new gear; maintaining it is just as important. Armor and clothing will degrade over time, requiring repairs using the right materials. Leather armor might require animal hides, while metal armor needs ingots and tools to patch up. Some materials are more durable than others—fur clothing provides warmth but wears out quickly, while reinforced plate armor lasts longer but is costly to maintain.

[h2]Rare & Legendary Gear[/h2]

While most armor and clothing are crafted from standard materials, there are rare and legendary pieces hidden throughout the world. These items offer unique stat bonuses or special effects, making them valuable finds for those who seek out Skye’s greatest challenges.

[h2]Crafting & Hunting for Materials[/h2]

Mostly armor and clothing aren’t simply found; they must be crafted using materials sourced from the world. Whether it’s hunting animals for leather and furs, mining ore for metal components, or gathering plant fibers for cloth, every piece of equipment has a crafting journey. Some advanced gear requires multiple crafted sub-components, adding depth to the game’s survival and crafting mechanics.

[h2]A New Layer of Strategy[/h2]

The addition of wearable equipment transforms Skye: Rebirth into a deeper survival experience. Players must now carefully plan their outfits based on the conditions and challenges they face. Will you gear up for combat, prioritize mobility, or prepare for a harsh winter night? The choice is yours.

Stay tuned for more updates as I continue refining and expanding the world of Skye! Let me know your thoughts, ideas and which armor pieces you’re most excited to craft!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/eff3409312a7b03a056563e461a1f9b57dface74.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/9f0a2195fda8f76e324ac8c22da310e6f416a4c6.png[/img]

[h3]Our journey has just begun![/h3]

- Mark

notes.title: Official Statement on Recent Claims & The Future of Skye: The Misty Isle
notes.content:
[h1]Official Statement on Recent Claims & The Future of Skye: The Misty Isle[/h1]
[hr][/hr]

I want to take a moment to directly address misleading claims circulating about Skye: The Misty Isle and my professional decisions. Normally, I would not respond to speculation, but due to the serious and misleading accusations I feel it is necessary to address these accusations.

[h2]Setting the Record Straight[/h2]
[hr][/hr]

[b]Skye Has Not Been Abandoned[/b]

While Skye: The Misty Isle has faced significant challenges, the project remains available, and I have always been transparent about its status. I fully acknowledge that Skye has fallen short of expectations, and I am actively working to address its issues.

The claim that Skye was a "cash grab" or that I intentionally misled the community is entirely false. The game was developed over several years with personal financial investment and dedication. Any suggestion of deception ignores the complexities of game development and the financial struggles that indie studios often face.

[h2]Addressing Claims of Dishonesty[/h2]
[hr][/hr]

There have been accusations that I "lied" about stepping away for personal reasons while continuing to work elsewhere. This is a gross misrepresentation of the facts:

[list]
[*] Revenue from Skye is legally designated for repaying creditors, including volunteers owed compensation.
[*] I cannot indefinitely work for free while meeting these obligations, which is why I have taken on another project to support myself and my team financially.
[*] The new project I am working on is not "a basically identical game." Skye is a survival game, while this new project is fundamentally different in scope, gameplay, and vision.
[/list]

[h2]Why Skye Remained on Steam[/h2]
[hr][/hr]

In October 2024, I resigned from Aurora Game Studios (AGS) due to an increasingly difficult internal work environment. Former team members themselves have acknowledged the challenges:

[i]"Our treatment of each other, especially Mark, has been disgusting. It broke my heart that the only way he could see to escape this vortex of baneful behavior was to walk away from his own company."

"This obsession with pretending to be a AAA studio, keeping the community at arm’s length and afraid to put anything out that's not super polished, is serving only to lose goodwill and undermine trust in us."[/i]

When I stepped away, I offered Skye and AGS to those remaining at the company, but no one chose to take over. Soon after, other team members also left, leaving me as the legal company director responsible for its closure.

Initially, the team discussed removing Skye: The Misty Isle from sale. However, in documentation provided during the company’s transition period, concerns were raised about the financial implications of doing so. The document stated:

"The decision to remove Skye: The Misty Isle from Steam’s store precludes the ability to generate further revenue that could have been allocated to repay creditors. While I understand that this will prevent poor reviews and player backlash due to abandonment of the game in an unoptimised state, this action effectively halts the game’s potential to fulfill its commercial promise and disregards the expectations of the player community."

While this was not a legally binding directive, it was a factor that contributed to the decision to keep the game available for purchase. The intention has always been to navigate these challenges responsibly, balancing financial obligations with the interests of players.

[h2]Regarding Deleted Steam Comments[/h2]
[hr][/hr]

Concerns have been raised about deleted Steam comments and posts. To clarify: these were removed by a volunteer due to personal privacy concerns following their resignation. However, I understand how this contributed to a sense of abandonment or a perception of attempting to suppress discussion.

[h2]What’s Next for Skye?[/h2]
[hr][/hr]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/012755610f61e65a33a737460d192821092bf90c.png[/img]

I had intended to announce this after completing more work, but given recent events, I feel it’s important to be fully transparent.

I have been working—when possible—to restore and improve Skye in line with its original hardcore survival vision. With so many changes coming to the core gameplay, Skye’s name will change to reflect this new beginning and a return to what made it appealing as a game originally.

After launch, a major patch was in development, but since some of the work was done by volunteers who were no longer contractually covered, their contributions had to be removed at their request. This rendered the game’s codebase non-functional. The only options were to revert Skye to its launch state or rebuild its core systems from scratch. I chose the latter.

[b]Current and planned Improvements include:[/b]

[list]
[*] Complete overhaul of core mechanics – Logging, harvesting, survival, clothing, heat management, world events, and environment interactions.
[*] A richer, more immersive world – Expanded exploration and interactivity.
[*] A brand-new UI, journaling system, and deeper world lore.
[*] Updated combat, farming, navigation, and multiplayer – One of the most requested features.
[*] Restoring six months of optimizations and fixes that were never released.
[*] Mod support – Encouraging community-driven content.
[/list]

I acknowledge that there has been another period of silence between December 2024 and March 2025. This was due to resolving financial and legal matters—something that is now behind me. Moving forward, I am committed to being more active on Discord and social platforms. Over the next few weeks, I will share video updates showcasing these improvements, rather than just screenshots. 

As an example of the visual overhaul coming alongside gameplay changes with "Rebirth", here is the same location in the game, [i]gameplay videos will follow[/i]:

[h3]Skye: The Misty Isle[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/37e192bcee5aec42dc0f0e2d15bb8a5e29555370.png[/img]
[h3]Skye: Rebirth[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/094322ded4cfb354a8ede9219820757c87d6acaf.png[/img]
[hr][/hr]
[h3]Other Screenshots[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/6e5a22788dd6a0c03fd7b3b459d7116a6dca7bb2.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/a04f412101e7b532e0c24ebe26796e0935d14041.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/854100cdeed0bdede952c8a63d2aee5c9acdd865.png[/img]

[h2]Beyond Skye[/h2]
[hr][/hr]

Some of us have founded Re\Vive, a new studio that allows us to continue our creative work free from the legal complications surrounding AGS. Putting creativity at the centre of production rather than bureaucracy.

Our new project, The Eternal Throne, is an entirely new combat-focused game, built from the ground up with no shared code or assets from Skye. It is an ambitious and distinct project in its own right.

I remain unapologetically supportive of the vision and creativity of those at Re\Vive. It is an exciting new studio dedicated to crafting meaningful, immersive experiences. The incredible team there has been working tirelessly to bring their game to life, and they do not deserve to be attacked by association. Like all indie developers, they are striving to break into an increasingly difficult industry.

Meanwhile, Skye will once again be my personal endeavor as I work to fulfill its original vision and honor my responsibilities to the community.

[h2]Final Thoughts[/h2]
[hr][/hr]

It is disappointing to be attacked for taking time to be with my family after working seven days a week for three years—especially when these attacks only harm my ability to repay company debts.

I understand that this statement may still be met with cynicism, but at this point, I cannot say anything without it being challenged, and I get that. Instead, my priority is to show you the work being done, bring Skye: Rebirth to the level I envisioned three years ago, and support an emerging team that is eager to create something new.

Thank you to those who continue to support independent development, despite its challenges.

[b]— Mark[/b]

notes.title: An Update on Skye: The Misty Isle and Aurora Game Studios
notes.content:
Firstly, I want to thank everyone who reached out with messages of support and understanding following our announcement in December regarding the closure of Aurora Game Studios and the end of active development on Skye: The Misty Isle. Your kindness, empathy, and encouragement have meant more than I can express during what has been an incredibly difficult time.

Since that announcement, there have been ongoing internal matters to resolve behind the scenes, including legal, financial, and operational challenges tied to winding down the company and ensuring the project was responsibly handled. These complexities have taken longer than anticipated to work through, and I want to apologise for the continued silence while those issues were addressed.

One of the key reasons Skye remained available for sale on Steam—despite our original intention to remove it—was due to legal and procedural constraints while these internal matters were ongoing. Reducing the price or delisting the game before resolving these issues wasn’t possible, and I understand how this may have caused frustration or confusion for those who had been following the project closely. I want to sincerely thank you for your patience and understanding during this time.

After much thought and consideration, I’ve made the decision to leave Skye: The Misty Isle available on Steam. While active development is still on hold and the studio itself is no longer operational in the traditional sense, I’ve chosen to keep the game accessible to our community, with the hope that it can still offer an enjoyable experience for those discovering it. Additionally, I want to reassure you that I will continue to monitor feedback and aim to address any critical issues or community concerns where possible, in the background, as time and resources allow. While I understand that I cannot convince all of you of my intentions, I assure you I have made this decision with my love of the game and Skye at the forefront.

In recognition of the game’s status and to make it more accessible, Skye’s price will be reduced to £9.99, with a further discount during the upcoming Steam Spring Sale, where it will be available for £4.99. I’ll continue to review this pricing over time to ensure it feels fair for both new players and those who have supported us from the beginning. I hope this makes it easier for more players to explore the Isle of Skye and experience what our small, passionate team worked so hard to build.

Though this is far from the ideal path I had once envisioned for Skye, I still believe in the heart of this project and what we created together. While there are no promises of a full return to development at this time, keeping the game available—and listening to those still playing—is the least I can do to honour the journey we’ve all shared. There is still a lot for me to do including updating the steam descriptions with relevant information but I am working through all of the Aurora channels so that the information about the game state is relevant and up to date.

Thank you again for standing by us. Your support, feedback, and care continue to keep the spirit of Skye alive.

With gratitude,
Mark
Founder, Aurora Game Studios

notes.title: Aurora Game Studios Announcement December 2024
notes.content:
First and foremost, I want to sincerely apologise for the lack of communication over the past few months. I understand it has been unfair to leave you without updates for so long. The truth is, that the future of the project has been in constant flux and filled with uncertainty. During this time, we’ve been working tirelessly to explore different options in the hope of keeping the game moving forward.

Three and a half years ago, while my wife and daughter were away for the weekend, I sat down at my desk with an idea, a name, and a dream—to create the kind of deep, immersive survival game I had always wanted to play. I still remember the moment my wife walked into the room when they returned, asking what I was up to. I told her, “Rather than playing games every night, I’ve decided to make one instead.”

What started as a personal challenge quickly became a shared journey. From learning the craft of game development to sharing each milestone with our growing community, I’ve been overwhelmed by the passion, creativity, and support you’ve shown. The project grew in scope and ambition because of you, and together we built something far beyond what I could have imagined during those early days.

Creating Skye: The Misty Isle has been a labour of love, and seeing the game come alive in Unreal Engine 5 was nothing short of remarkable. From crafting the intricate details of Skye and Mørsvikbotn to perfecting gameplay mechanics that honoured the Viking spirit, every step was a mix of challenge and joy. I’ll never forget moments like launching our first internal build on Steam or the hilarity of our first community livestream, where a spawning bug gave us all the unforgettable Wilbur.

But this journey has not been without its struggles. Developing an indie game of this scale brought immense financial pressure and required personal sacrifices from everyone on the team. Despite countless promising conversations with investors and publishers, we were never able to secure the funding needed to complete the game and as such entirely self-funded development out of our own pockets. This left us operating under a near-constant crunch, with many of us working 80+ hour weeks, sacrificing time with our families to keep the dream alive.

I’ll always remember the words of my daughter, who was just one year old when I began this journey and four at launch. She told me, “You haven’t done anything with us as a family since I was two.” That moment hit me hard. Despite all our efforts, and even with the launch of Early Access—a decision born of necessity—we found ourselves launching alongside much larger, more polished titles, struggling to gain the traction needed to sustain the project.

On paper, the launch was a success: only 16% of indie teams make it to release, and we sat in the top 20% of best-selling games on Steam. Yet, the harsh reality is that only the top 8% of games on the platform generate sustainable revenue. The reality post-launch is that none of the team has been able to be paid, myself included and we have not generated enough income to cover the personal expenses incurred during development let alone sustain a future for the business.

As such and after much reflection, I’ve made the incredibly difficult decision to stop production on Skye: The Misty Isle and disbanding Aurora Game Studios. This is not the outcome I had hoped for, but continuing under these circumstances is no longer sustainable—for the team or me personally. I have a young family to look out for, and at this time, I need to prioritise my own and their well-being.

We do have one final update to share. Over the past six months, we’ve been working hard on an overhaul and bug-fixing patch, which will include significant improvements to farming mechanics, over 130 bug fixes, and 40 quality-of-life updates. For those who already own the game, it will remain accessible in your libraries, but we will be removing it from sale on Steam as a recognition that production is ceasing.

To everyone who has supported us on this journey—our amazing community, the dedicated team members who shared this dream, and every player who set sail with us—I cannot thank you enough. Your enthusiasm, feedback, and belief in this project brought Skye: The Misty Isle to life in ways I never could have imagined.

While this chapter of Aurora Game Studios is coming to a close, I deeply believe this isn’t the end of Skye’s story. The heart of the game remains a dream I hold close, and I hope to return to it one day under brighter circumstances.

As I’ve reflected on these last weeks and the question my daughter posed to me, “What happened to your game Daddy?” someone close to the project shared a saying with me: “Man trifft sich immer zweimal im Leben” – “You meet each other at least twice in a lifetime.” I will share that sentiment with my daughter and carry it with me as I take the next steps forward.

Thank you, from the bottom of my heart, for everything.

With deepest gratitude,

Mark
Founder, Aurora Game Studios

notes.title: Demo Performance Update
notes.content:
[b]Hej Víkingar![/b]

We can't thank you all enough for the feedback you have given us over the last week on our demo. We have heard and understood your concerns and have now [b]published an update[/b] that should address many of the issues you have been experiencing.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Performance Update[/h3]

This patch has covered the following:
[list]
    [*] [b]Landscape[/b]
Our newly scaled landscape was introduced in Patch 0.2.8, which seemed to be causing some performance issues. We have done a huge optimisation pass on the textured which should reduce this impact and resolve the issues.
    [*] [b]Metahumans[/b]
We discovered that our new Metahuman models were attempting to render textures at a very high level, which was causing large performance hitches. We have now significantly scaled-down these details, which reduces the impact of loading in these character models.
    [*] [b]Nanite[/b]
We have been made aware of some issues surrounding Nanite loading, which was causing a significant bottleneck for many systems. As there is currently no available fix for this in our current engine version, we have decided to [b]disable Nanite by default[/b] until we can address the issues.
[/list]
In our testing, these changes have [b]achieved an additional 30FPS across most systems and specs[/b].

We will continue to gather feedback on performance and promote improvements as often as possible to ensure players have the best possible in-game experience.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Demo Availability[/h3]

We have made the decision to [b]keep our demo live[/b] for the foreseeable Early Access period. The demo will be [b]updated with the most stable version[/b] of the base game and will include performance, optimisation, and quality-of-life updates as they become available. While the playable area in the demo will not expand, this will allow players to track our progress through development and personally [b]experience the game for free before deciding to buy[/b].

We want to ensure that every player is fully informed throughout all stages of our development and can share their feedback and experiences. We are committed to transparency and want to ensure that all players are happy with the game in its currently available state before making the decision to purchase.

We understand the challenges of entering public access at such an early stage in development. However, as a small, self-publishing team of only five, [b]community feedback is vital[/b] to helping us make the game the best it can possibly be. We will continue to post regular updates documenting our progress, and we want everyone to have access to this journey without financial commitment.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Early Access Pricing[/h3]

We have now published our [b]pricing for Early Access[/b], which will be set to [b]£20.99 GBP ($24.99 USD)[/b]. However, we will [b]launch with a 20% discount[/b] as a thank you for all the feedback and understanding you have shown us over the demo period. As we continue to develop the game, this price will be [b]subject to change[/b] to reflect its quality and the expansion of the content available.

We would like to thank you all once again for your support over the last three years. We hope to see you all on the Isle soon and can't wait to continue this development journey into Early Access with you!


[hr][/hr]
Stay tuned for more updates and patch notes soon!

notes.content:
[b]Hej Víkingar![/b]

Welcome to our first Production Department update! Take a look behind the scenes with our Production department as they share insight into the evolution of the game. 

From in-depth mechanic showcases revealing key gameplay to an exclusive chat with the dev team on the future plans of Skye: The Misty Isle!

[hr][/hr]
[previewyoutube=XRA6D73-Xtw;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Early Access World Showcase[/h3]

We revealed a flythrough of the breathtaking landscapes of Morsvikbotn, Norway, and explored the vibrant towns nestled within its majestic embrace! Our starting map in Skye: The Misty Isle features the fictional town of Ravndal as its bustling hub, where adventure awaits around every corner.

For our final day, we revealed a flythrough of Norway's breathtaking, hyper-realistic landscapes, and explored the vibrant towns nestled within its majestic embrace! Our starting location in Skye: The Misty Isle features the fictional town of Ravndal, a charming settlement nestled amidst the rugged terrain of Mørsvikbotn. Perched on the world's edge, it boasts unparalleled views of the vast Nordfolda fjord.

[hr][/hr]
[previewyoutube=waj1WU6QPrY;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Early Access Feature Showcase 1[/h3]

Kicking off the week with our first of three mechanic showcases, we demonstrate in-game footage of our dev testing area, displaying mechanics such as foraging, forestry, mining ores, farming, collectables, and fishing! 

[b]Foraging[/b]
Explore diverse biomes and map-specific locations to uncover essential resources crucial for crafting and sustenance in the wild.

[b]Forestry[/b]
Venture into dense forests, harvesting wood for crafting while facing challenges like confrontations with wolves. Utilise tools like knives to enhance resource-gathering efficiency.

[b]Mining[/b]
Delve into underground mines to unearth a wealth of ores, including coal, copper, and iron. Refine your findings at blacksmiths or trade them for profit amidst threats like bandits.

[b]Farming[/b]
Cultivate crops in customisable plots, engage in trading at bustling markets, and harvest your yield for sustenance or cooking, influencing the landscape of survival.

[b]Collectables[/b]
Discover over 200 unique items scattered throughout the world, crafting them into essential components and advanced gear to shape the narrative of your journey.

[b]Fishing[/b]
Cast your line in serene wilderness spots or bustling piers, reel in a variety of fish, and savour the fruits of your labour with a hearty meal, enhancing your survival experience.

Click the links to read more!

[url=https://www.instagram.com/p/C7esE8coV7v/?img_index=1/]Instagram[/url] | [url=https://www.facebook.com/share/v/V8KR89JEDh6JGRmd/]Facebook[/url]

[hr][/hr]
[previewyoutube=ljtA2uN5Ve4;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Early Access Feature Showcase 2[/h3]

Our second mechanics showcase covered our primitive to advanced crafting system using workbenches, trading with our 14 specialised vendors, cooking gathered ingredients, building from our modular build parts, and customising your builds with decorations and melee and ranged combat. 

[b]Crafting[/b]
Hone your crafting skills, starting with primitive items and expanding your abilities with various workbenches. Forge higher-tier components to thrive in the wilderness and overcome challenges.

[b]Workbenches[/b]
Explore a variety of 20 different workstations scattered across the land. 

[b]Traders[/b]
Interact with 14 specialised vendors to acquire or craft 211 essential items crucial for your journey's success.

[b]Cooking[/b]
Gather ingredients through foraging, hunting, and farming endeavours. Utilise fire or cooking workbenches to prepare nourishing meals, sustaining yourself amidst the wilderness's rigours.

[b]Building[/b]
Unleash your creativity with modular build parts crafted from wood or stone. Construct a permanent home or shelter, establishing your presence in the vast and ever-changing world.

[b]Decorations[/b]
Customise your surroundings with an array of workbenches, usable items such as beds, and decorative elements, including shelves, fur rugs, and tables. Make your space truly your own.

[b]Combat[/b]
Craft melee and ranged weapons to defend yourself against threats ranging from bandits to wild animals. Engage in thrilling battles, securing your survival and dominance in the challenging landscape.

Click the links to read more!

[url=https://www.instagram.com/p/C7hZeeWtODC/?img_index=1/]Instagram[/url] | [url=https://www.facebook.com/share/v/xE7VNBCdx6dBcvxo/]Facebook[/url]

[hr][/hr]
[previewyoutube=3iIrjP9YO30;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Early Access Feature Showcase 3[/h3]

Our third and final mechanic showcase showed traversal through vaulting and climbing, horse-riding and sailing. We also revealed our day-to-night cycles and dynamic weather, such as fog, rain and snow.

[b]Traversal[/b]
Navigate the terrain with agility using vaulting, climbing, and nimble dodge and roll techniques. Embrace excitement with exhilarating zipline rides across the wilderness.

[b]Riding[/b]
Embark on epic journeys by hiring horses from stables, utilising their speed and strength for travel across the expansive world. Harness their power in combat when necessary, ensuring your dominance.

[b]Time and Weather[/b]
Witness the ever-changing dynamics of day and night, accompanied by dynamic weather phenomena such as fog, rain, and snow. Utilise the real-world night sky for navigation beneath the stars.

[b]Sailing[/b]
Explore vast lakes and oceans, freely swimming or commanding large longships to conquer the seas. Let the call of the waves guide your journey across the waters, unlocking new horizons and adventures.

Click the links to read more!

[url=https://www.instagram.com/p/C7j1qceNWFL/?img_index=1/]Instagram[/url] | [url=https://www.facebook.com/share/v/gBXHWDzS8Eq6573N/]Facebook[/url]

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Procedural Content Showcase[/h3]

We revealed a behind the scenes look at Unreal Engine’s PCG technology that is powering our procedural towns and forests. From settlements and NPCs to decorations and foliage, enjoy in-engine images revealing the inner workings of the game’s environments.

[b]Mesh Scatter[/b]
We've begun using new Procedural Scattering on static meshes. Here, you can see how clustered static meshes adapt to concave surfaces, creating organic plant growth. This method allows for natural-looking procedural content with customisable parameters, giving us greater creative control over the final product.

[b]Towns and NPCs[/b]
Procedural technology helps us bring structures, roads, and environmental elements to life, creating immersive locations for players to explore. Our NPC and Enemy placement, largely driven by data tables, dictates spawn points and emergent behaviours to make the world feel truly alive.

[b]Forests and Foliage[/b]
We use a blend of Unreal Engine 5’s technologies to shape our environmental design. From the strategic placement and lush growth of foliage, guided by procedural rules and datasets, to the use of Nanite technology, we've amplified density and realism in our environments like never before.

[b]Fences and Decorations[/b]
We've also started exploring the use of Procedural Content Generation tools for our fences, decorating our world with grass, foliage, and rocks that spawn along the edges of splines, creating a natural and overgrown aesthetic.

[b]Environmental Effects[/b]
We also use a more traditional approach to procedural content, randomisation for natural environmental effects. Utilising 'weighted' points, depicted by the grey boxes, along with randomised scaling and rotation, helps us break up the monotony of flat surfaces. This method enables us to scatter ground elements like rocks, stones, leaves, and debris, bypassing the constraints of traditional grass layers in landscape design.

[h3]Department Update[/h3]

Our Production Department provided an update on what they have been working on recently, from rolling out over 500 updates since April to diving deep into the intricacies of a full map overall and MetaHuman integration. 

Expand or click the links to read more!

[expand type=details]
[b]What We’re Working On[/b] 

Over the past few months, we have been busier than ever. Since April, we’ve rolled out over 500 updates to our game’s internal branch! It’s been a real team effort, with everyone helping out with fixes, changes and improvements. 

We’ve been hard at work overhauling our artificial intelligence systems, implementing our MetaHumans, redesigning the user interface and maps, and, of course, handling all the bugs and technical issues that follow. 

[b]Our Favourite Project[/b]

Our most interesting focus was integrating MetaHumans. It's been a pretty big task and needed hard work from everyone on the team, but seeing these characters come to life with their quirky expressions and subtle, true-to-life, movements has been so rewarding.

As we continue to explore the possibilities in Unreal Engine 5, we're really excited about the potential to enhance the game, and each step forward brings us closer to our goals of hyper-realism and immersion.

[b]Our Biggest Challenge[/b]

One of our biggest challenges has been redesigning the user interface. There’s such a delicate balance of minimalism, functionality and artistic theme, and it has been a tough process for all of us, across every department.

We’re so happy with the progress we’ve made, despite the steep learning curve! We’re excited for players to see what we’ve made and to get their insights into other improvements we can make as we continue.

[b]What We’ve Learnt[/b] 

Optimisation has also been a major hurdle for us, mainly with our maps. We recently scaled down our 8k heightmaps to tackle the performance issues caused by a landscape made of over 64 million polygons! We dropped the resolution to 2k, which gave us huge framerate improvements but, unfortunately, resulted in a landscape of jagged edges and navigation issues. 

So, after all that work, we had to scale the resolution back up to 4k, giving us a landscape with only 16 million polygons - a 4x reduction from the original! This gave us the stable framerate we needed while allowing us a clean slate to completely redesign both maps with higher-quality textures, and better environmental design. We've been fighting a constant, uphill battle to balance visual fidelity and stable performance throughout development but, finally, we seem to be winning.

[b]Latest Technology[/b]

The constant challenge of working with cutting-edge technology has been an interesting process. We began work in Unreal Engine 5 before its public release and, while it’s been a really exciting time, it also means we’re working with an ever-adapting production process to keep up with an evolving engine, and unforeseen bugs, issues and errors are just part of that process.

However, for all of the complexities and occasional setbacks, our experience of Unreal Engine 5 has been so incredibly rewarding, and has allowed us to explore new creative possibilities and push the boundaries of what's achievable for our small team.

[b]The Community[/b]

Since February 2023, we've been gathering insights from our dedicated group of Æsir testers, on everything from mechanics and gameplay to world-building and aesthetics. As a small team, player feedback has been so helpful and we’re so excited to expand our community as we continue to grow. 

We’ve already started to open up dialogue with our wider community, especially over on our discord server. This has been so useful in helping us prioritise different aspects of development to meet players’ expectations.

[b]Looking into the Future[/b]

We're so excited for the future of our team, and the ambitions and plans we have for the game are a long journey that we can’t wait to tackle with our community. 

We know that development is a long process and we understand how frustrating it can be for players to wait for updates or development phases. But, even after three years, this is just the beginning!
[/expand]

[h3]Svartalfheim[/h3]

[i]"Svartalfheim's subterranean landscapes are adorned with intricate craftsmanship, showcasing the expertise of its dwarf and craftsmen inhabitants. This phase aligns with early development work, akin to craftsmen constructing the foundational elements of the project with precision and attention to detail."[/i]

Following the initial iteration and fixing stage of our closed Pre-Alpha, April 2023 marks the next phase of development. With the foundations laid and hundreds of bugs fixed, we implemented further enhancements and refinements, shifting our focus to improving mechanics, polishing environments and optimising performance

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Helheim[/h3]

[i]"Helheim is the Norse underworld, a realm of shadow and mystery where the souls of the departed dwell. It is a place of transition and transformation. This initial phase represents ideas in their early, formative state, as the developers explore various possibilities and lay the foundational groundwork for the project."[/i]

From the start of development in June 2021 to our closed Pre-Alpha launch on 24th February 2023 and beyond, this main development phase built the foundations of the game and saw significant updates to a wide range of features, led by the feedback and support of our Æsir donators. 

Whilst we are unable to post the details of every change, largely due to the lack of documentation during our early stages and the limitations of character count, we wanted to share just a little preview of the work we have done behind the scenes.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]0.1.0[/h3]

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Department Update[/h3]

Our Art Department provided an update on what they have been working on recently, including historical research, working outside of their comfort zone and what the focus will be in the future. 

Expand or click the links to read more!

[expand type=details]
[b]What We're Working On[/b]

We have been very busy in the art department over the last few months. Our main focus has been chipping away at a huge overhaul of the user interface; icons, maps, menus, you name it, we’ve done it!

Alongside this, we have been teaming up with the narrative department to start bringing our characters to life; exploring early face and hair sketches to reimagine in MetaHumans and, as ever, we have been neck-deep in research.

[b]Our Favourite Project[/b]

Bringing Einar and Sissel to life, from first initial concepts through various iterations of their MetaHumans, has been such an interesting process. While we are still working within the limits of our small team, it was great to see some of these characters start to be realised.

Knowing that they will continue to evolve during development and as our resources and capabilities increase is something to look forward to, and we can’t wait to share these changes with you!

[b]Our Biggest Challenge[/b]

The biggest challenge so far was making the Æsir shield. It was very important to us to have the actual shield in-game and ready for our Early Access launch.

As we have some very basic experience with 3D modelling, we decided to take the plunge into learning Blender to model the shield from scratch. Nothing beats the sense of accomplishment when you see your own asset in-game for the first time!

[b]What We've Learnt[/b]

We have learnt so much over the years, tackling work outside our comfort zone and acquiring new skills to really push the game forward. Recently, we have spent a lot of time in-engine, helping the production department by redesigning some locations and points of interest in the game.

As a small team, we get the opportunity to learn more behind-the-scenes aspects of game development that we wouldn’t normally get to see or enjoy in our respective roles.

[b]Geographical and Historical Accuracy[/b]

Historical accuracy is very important to us, and something that is always on our minds. Research is a constant theme of development, but knowing when to push the boundaries for visuals is also vital.

We want the game to look visually recognisable for its time period, while also maintaining a respectful and realistic portrayal of the cultures that we are exploring. We are still finding the difficult balance of adhering to historical accuracy, without sacrificing the iconic Viking aesthetic.

[b]Looking to the Future[/b]

In the future, we will be focusing our attention on the game’s visuals, starting with redesigning our placeholder assets and bringing our characters and the world around them to life. 

We can’t wait to begin creating a unique identity for both Norway and Skye, their different cultures, and to see the game take on such a huge visual overhaul throughout development.
[/expand]

notes.title: Department Update | May 2024
notes.content:
[b]Hej Víkingar![/b]

Welcome to our first Narrative Department update! Take a look behind the scenes with our Narrative Department as they give us the inside scoop on their work over the last few months. 

From crafting exciting adventures to the challenges of working within real history, the team shares their triumphs, struggles, and everything in-between to help you step into the enchanting world of Skye: The Misty Isle!

[hr][/hr]
[previewyoutube=0eN4NzR96MI;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]The Orphan[/h3]

The highlight of our week was the reveal of our main protagonist, Einar, in Metahuman form. We were excited to get him in-game, replacing our longstanding, Pre-Alpha placeholder. No doubt he will continue to go through many more iterations in the future.

[table noborder=1]
    [tr]
        [td][img=inline]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/457f743cfb99104644c12888f9de09e0bc4f2345.png[/img][/td]
        [td]　[/td]
        [td][i]"Born the son of no one and left to the gods in the bough of an old tree, it was there he received his first name, one that would be uttered far beyond the shores of his birth for ages to come.
Einar.

Found by the barren shield-maiden, Solfrid, and her husband, he was proclaimed a gift and returned with them to the valley nestled town of Ravndal, home of Clan Sváfnir. Placed in ritual within the embrace of the ancient tree, Bólormr, Einar was welcomed as a new son of the clan and remained in the care of Solfrid.

Raised to be a prolific hunter like his father and a formidable fighter like his mother, Einar’s curiosity was nurtured and encouraged to extend far beyond the bounds of Ravndal.
His ambition, the whispers of prophecy, and the secrets of his past would steer him far from the reach of Ravndal."[/i][/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
Click the links to read more!

[url=https://www.instagram.com/p/C6WmX32pP4T/]Instagram[/url] | [url=https://www.facebook.com/SkyeTheMistyIsle/posts/pfbid028zWyBXZRxQfnhfUZ32QSKXd8MuhvNywf2Ef4xt4MCrnS9aTACRMcMNvGqEuT9YTvl/]Facebook[/url]

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Ravndal, Mørsvikbotn[/h3]

We explored the rich history of Ravndal, our fictional Viking settlement nestled in the breathtaking vistas of Mørsvikbotn, Norway. From its humble beginnings to the present day, Ravndal is a testament to the resilience and spirit of its people. 

As our starting location, Ravndal is where we have spent a lot of time recently rebuilding ready for Early Access, and narrative week was the perfect time to introduce you to the lore of the settlement.

[table noborder=1]
    [tr]
        [td][img=inline]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/0ebb67f043d184843cec82465c739d92259cf9d6.png[/img][/td]
        [td]　[/td]
        [td][i]"Ravndal, nestled on the shores of the Nordfolda fjord, is the proud home of the Ætt Sváfnir. Built around the ancient tree of Bólormr, it is a hub of fishing and trade. The town is stretched across the shape of the shore, with the homes of the oldest families standing in a circle beneath the great looming tree.

It was founded nearly a hundred years ago by a fisherman and his son. The fisherman, Alvis, had lost his way while out hunting and had used the sun to try and guide him back north. They stumbled across a fjord and discovered the old tree that stood alone from the woods."[/i][/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
Click the links to read more!

[url=https://www.instagram.com/p/C6bvZX7gQym/]Instagram[/url] | [url=https://www.facebook.com/SkyeTheMistyIsle/posts/pfbid0AU2hPSR8JRptZCHeka9FgRTZRpTk99LZ2vtkiof9VLMUaR9qxJUrHP2ekQqM7B8ul/]Facebook[/url]

[hr][/hr]
[h3]The Seer[/h3]

We introduced Sissel, the wise and enigmatic clan seer whose prophetic insights will guide you to the misty landscapes of Skye. With a demand for blood as her price for truth, Sissel is as fascinating as she is foreboding. 

She is one of many named NPCs we started to realise in Metahumans, ready for Early Access, and one who will feature in the days to come. 

[table noborder=1]
    [tr]
        [td][img=inline]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/1b523e06a7c9942f5d528eb9e9fa04c0f75d8146.png[/img][/td]
        [td]　[/td]
        [td][i]"Her name was Sissel, the third-born daughter of a third-born daughter, touched with the prophetic gift her foremothers possessed. She was raised far from Ravndal, originating from the borders of Nóregr and Finnland, though her journey from childhood to seeress remains largely shrouded in mystery.

Hailed a frightening curiosity, Sissel proved an invaluable asset to the people of clan Sváfnir after she appeared one day beneath the great tree of Bólormr, foretelling of a terrible winter that would soon plague their lands and decimate their crops. Sissel demanded the people of Ravndal must pay her price each time they desired to know their truth and be warned of their trials.

Her price was always blood."[/i][/td]

[h3]Department Update[/h3]

Our Narrative Department provided a general update on their progress, offering insights into their collaboration with the Art Department, their commitment to historical accuracy, and the challenges and joys of world-building.

Expand or click the links to read more!

[expand type=details]
[b]What We're Working On[/b]

Over the past few months, the team has been working very hard on developing the exciting opening tutorial and establishing the key characters that players will initially interact with in the starting zone of Ravndal, Mørsvikbotn. 

We have also been working closely with the Art Department to transform some of our characters from ideas into reality, delving into Unreal Engine 5 and its latest MetaHuman technology. We hope that players are as excited to see our creations come to life as we are, and can’t wait to show more soon.

[b]Geographical and Historical Accuracy[/b]

We’re dedicated to creating a game that is rooted in geographical and historical accuracy. Aside from occasional creative liberties to ensure an exciting and engaging visual experience, we remain committed to making ‘Skye’ as accurate as we can. 

With this in mind, we’ve evaded any heavily mythological elements, however, that’s not to say that Gods won’t play a part in the actions of our characters. Faith in their beliefs was a defining part of cultures of that time and we have made an effort to reflect that in our story and characters. 

[b]Our Biggest Challenge[/b]

Working within history creates several challenges, whether it’s the restrictions of real locations or finding accounts of historical events, writing in a period as partially documented as the Dark Ages can be both a blessing and a curse when it comes to deciding what might have been. 

Building a world that fits into reality has been difficult but we have worked hard to establish unique environments that bring to life our characters and lore, while committing to recreating the iconic locations of Norway and Skye.

[b]Our Favourite Project[/b]

Our main character, Einar, has been the most endearing to write about. We’ve worked carefully to bring to life a protagonist worthy of such a large game while still maintaining an edge of uniqueness to his qualities and personality. 

However, the most fun has been in developing the world in which our story will unfold and creating a rich history, spanning generations before Einar’s journey. Creating the characters that make up his world, their lore and histories, and carving out a piece of Norway for our tale has been a gift to experience. 

[b]Looking to the Future[/b]

Throughout development, the depth of our story has expanded massively, but we remain focused on providing a balanced experience between both story-driven content and classic open-world survival. ‘Skye: The Misty Isle’ is going to put a fresh spin on the survival game genre, blending linear storytelling with sandbox freedom.

We're very excited to share our epic storyline with our players and let them explore the expansive world of ‘Skye’ with a purpose and goal. We're not just making a game; we're giving them a real experience to immerse themselves in.

notes.title: Development Update | May 2024
notes.content:
[b]Greetings Víkingar![/b]

We'd like to start with an honest apology to all of you. It's been too long since we've spoken, and for that, we're truly sorry. We understand the frustration that comes with our silence, and we want to shed some light on why we've been so quiet.

The truth is, it's been a bit of a journey for us behind the scenes. For those of you who don't know, we're a team of only five people. For three years now, we've been battling constant challenges. Whether it's the relentless strain of tight resources and even tighter budgets, the endless quest to keep up with ever-evolving technology, or the fair share of personal hardships we've each faced along the way, it's been a tough ride and things rarely go as planned. Sometimes, we hit roadblocks; other times, we get so lost in the work that we forget to lift our heads and share our journey with you.

We've been doing our best to stay active on social media, but we understand that might not have reached all of you here on Steam. We're a new company, finding our way, and we're still learning what works best for each platform. We've seen your comments and heard your frustrations, and, moving forward, we will try to be more active and open - especially here on Steam. We want to do better. We want to be more than just a studio; we want to be a community. We want to connect with you more and to share this journey - the highs and the lows - to make sure that you're a part of it, every step of the way.

Our Discord server is always open for a chat, a question, or even a friendly hello and, for those of you who are interested, you can also follow our progress over on our website and our socials.

Thank you, from the bottom of our hearts, for your support, patience, and understanding, and for sticking with us while we figure this out. We will be back very soon, so keep an eye out for more updates in the coming weeks!


Catch up soon,

The Aurora Team 🌙
[i](Mark, Aiden, Maddie, Lydia & Lauren)[/i]

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/0df267f3e678dd3abca1401e2088fd83c566ec91.png[/img]
[hr][/hr]
[b]Greetings Víkingar![/b]

The Pre-Alpha has been out for over 2 months within [b]NDA[/b] and things are progressing well! Our team have been working hard since launch and has released 12 patches since launch! Each patch has brought a plethora of bug fixes, (wonderfully reported by our excellent [b]Æsir[/b]), performance and visual upgrades, and numerous new, updated, or improved features too! 

A select few of which we'll share with you here:

[h3]Environments[/h3]
The entirety of the Skye and Norway levels have been reworked, meaning that terrain is 2x more accurate to real life and 4x more optimised than before.

[h3]Quests[/h3]
We have entirely reworked the journal and quest system. With this, we can bring forward some of the more basic quests that otherwise wouldn't have been included at this stage.

[h3]Hunger & Thirst[/h3]
We flicked the "on" switch for hunger and thirst, meaning that planning ahead for any potentially perilous journeys is now a must.

[h3]Animation[/h3]
The player and horse models have had an upgrade, both now using Inverse Kinematics (IK) rigs. This means our models' feet conform and dynamically adjust to the landscape instead of clipping through it.

[h3]Hunting[/h3]
Hunting has been added, with a minimum of 24 hunting locations now available across both Norway and Skye, and over 16 different types of animals to hunt.

This is only a small glimpse into the additions since we first launched. While we're under [b]NDA[/b], the complete patch notes are only available on Discord to our [b]Æsir[/b] supporters who continue to show us love and support and who have provided us with their valuable feedback every step of the way!


Skål,

notes.title: Development Update | Feb 2023
notes.content:
[b]Greetings Víkingar![/b]

Welcome to the Pre-Alpha Update! Here, we bring you with us on our journey as we venture from the lands of Norway, across the perilous seas to the newfound lands!

We will be opening our Pre-Alpha on [b]24/02/23[/b], join our Discord to find out more!

[hr][/hr]
[h3]The Pledge[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/0911f78ee701230bfdb093345e982ffc29102cd0.png[/img]

Our mighty Æsir have pledged themselves to the raiding party of Einar Ericsson and his plans to venture westwards from his clan home in Norway!

We ask that our fellow Víkingar burn their lamps bright and pay their tributes well, the Æsir will need all the fortune they can muster as they begin preparations for their journey west!

[hr][/hr]
[h3]The Plan[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/dea0b8769390d61dc41fd0ea3b88ec311ca81487.png[/img]

[i]"An opportunity has arisen, a boat; heading for the isles in the west. My father’s path. Mother insists he is dead, it pains her every time she must remind me. Yet that feeling inside has never ebbed.

He’s out there, somewhere, and now is my chance. Am I chasing Eikþyrnir as he did, or is the great stag of Valhalla leading me to my destiny?"[/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h3]The Journey[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/5a6c428ece261246030da633cb20d481581f6e54.png[/img]

[i]"We’ve been sailing for what seems like forever but every wave looks the same. Where is this land we’re headed for? Will we ever reach it?"[/i]

[h3]The Peril[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40987671/5681a6fddd80768504e3fabef9fb81dcb05d6171.png[/img]

[i]"Over a week at sea, nothing but dark clouds roared above us. For days this storm has raged with lightning tearing the sky apart - have we angered the gods?

Arkin claims we sail through Skotlandsfjörð, but the sea around us looks no different than the lands we have just left. The air is cold, and the wind stings my skin as the beating waves around us raise the boat high into the air.

We’ve lost two men already to the stormy waters below; how many more will it claim before we reach land? I fear no one watches over our journey into the west."[/i]

notes.title: Development Update | Jan 2023
notes.content:
[b]Greetings Víkingar![/b]

We wanted to take a moment to both reflect on 2022 and also acknowledge that the game did not release this year as we had hoped. We made significant progress on the version 0.3 release and completed all of the necessary work to get us to launch, but we were unable to resolve some bugs and continuity issues with map transitions before the end of the year.

The main issue for us has been with the loading and performance of the game, which we have been working to improve by migrating to the UE5 World Partition system and coming so close to finishing before Christmas. We managed to reduce the loading time from around 6 minutes to 5 seconds which solved the worst of the issues but we couldn't get through the last of the World Partition migration niggles in time.

We understand that delays can be frustrating, and we want to apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused. We are committed to delivering a high-quality game as soon as possible, that has always been the goal, and we will be continuing to work on it over the holiday season. We are hopeful that we will be able to launch the Pre-Alpha very early in 2023.

We want to thank you all for your patience and support as we continue to develop the game. The scope of the release has grown significantly since we first started, and we now have multiple game modes, creative and hardcore options, two new huge maps to explore, and a whole host of new traversal and game mechanics. 

Looking back on the 0.1 version we started last year, which we still have and only included the 16sqkm test map we had first created, the game has come a long way. We are excited to finally share this journey with all of you and look forward to stepping foot on the Misty Isle together!


Skål,

The Aurora Team 🌙
